diagram_math_checks.check: All pairs are primitive. det((1,0),(0,1))=1; det((0,1),(-1,-1))=1; det((-1,-1),(1,0))=1. Thus the Definition line 41 absolute-determinant formula gives all three geometric intersection numbers equal to one. The left blue arrows end at these exact coordinate pairs.

The slope supplier defines (p,q) modulo simultaneous sign, and boundary intersection mu dot lambda=-1. The caption explicitly calls the arrows coordinate vectors rather than oriented torus curves, so the +1 coordinate determinants are not misidentified as boundary-oriented algebraic intersections. Subscripts denote cyclic positions rather than numeric surgery coefficients.

Y_j=E_K(s_j) uses the exact filling objects of Definition line 41. Explicit directed edges are Y0 to Y1, Y1 to Yinfinity, Yinfinity to Y0: one incoming and one outgoing edge at each of the three vertices, matching the stated cyclic cobordism order. The actual native image visibly contains all three edges. These are cobordisms, not maps between Floer groups; no commutativity, exactness, or degree is asserted.

The existing Definition lines 43–51, including spectral-flow grading and translation dimension convention, remain unchanged. No analytic construction, graded Floer map, or exact triangle is introduced. This definition has no supplied proof; all rigorous definitions and subsequent theorem obligations remain independent of the figure.
